label: GitHub Code 2025 — Python
description: Real-world GitHub Python source files (the "content" field), streamed and sampled to 5,000 documents from a 55-language, 143M-row code corpus.
highlight: Real GitHub Python source code — a very different shape from the other three profiles, which are all prose or math. The content-type heuristic correctly identifies about 99.5% of documents here as code (versus roughly 90% on the math dataset), and nearly all ghost-token hits are code that legitimately manipulates tokenizer special tokens — checking for <|endoftext|>, mocking a tokenizer's <bos>/<eos> — rather than dataset contamination. The exceptions are [prompt] and [cls]: false positives from ordinary Python identifiers (a list literal, a class-method parameter) that happen to overlap with the ghost-token vocabulary.
finding: A file's embedded HTML fooled the extraction stage into treating the whole file as a scraped webpage, silently discarding most of its actual code. Fixed with a new --content-hint not-html flag that disables HTML tag stripping entirely for known code sources — even "lightweight" stripping was unsafe here, since <...> is common Python syntax (Flask routes, comparisons, generics), not markup.
facts: 28.9M rows (Python config); 143.7M rows across all 55 languages
